title: Institution
description: The accredited organisation that owns or awards a Programme.

localName.description: The institution's name in its own language.

places.description: Campuses, in the order a student would think of them.

about.description: Two or three concrete, non-promotional sentences.

codes.description: Identifiers a student has to type into a portal.

languageOfInstruction.description: Institution-level availability is context, never proof that a given Programme is taught in English.

media.description: A logo identifies; it does not license. Permission is never inferred from public visibility.

usageBasis.description: open-graph-linked: the institution's own share image, hot-linked from its server. free-licence-hosted: a freely licensed file we host and credit.

support.description: Explorable without a student disclosing anything about themselves.

ibEquivalences.description: The institution's own published additions to its Destination's Recognition Scheme: IB subjects (or a combination) it accepts for a local-scale subject. Read by the eligibility engine and the requirement wording before the national table's "no equivalent", so Aarhus's "Global Politics HL: Recognised as Social Science B" is a rule, not a note.

accepts.description: Alternatives; each is a list of IB subjects that must all be held. `ibLevel` is the lowest IB level that counts: SL means SL or HL.

jurisdiction.description: Which of its Destination’s Application Jurisdictions this institution admits under.

sector.description: Which of the Destination’s sectorLandscape routes this institution belongs to, by localName.

admissionRoutes.description: The institution's admission routes other than ranking on the converted average, as it publishes them — what a student below a quota 1 floor can still do. Read by the eligibility engine for 'which way in is left'.

short.description: The route in a few words, for a card line: "SDU's entrance test".

levelRaise.description: How this institution lets a student add a subject level they lack (supplementary courses, conditional admission), where it publishes its own terms. Overrides the Recognition Scheme's national text. `text` is subject-neutral; a text that names a subject goes under `subjects` (round 4: ITU's Maths sentence was shown to a student missing Danish A). scripts/test-eligibility.mjs fails if the action for one subject names another.

text.description: What the institution accepts, for any subject. Names no subject.

subjects.description: What the institution accepts for one subject, in its own words, used in place of `text` for that subject.

subject.description: The subject on the Recognition Scheme's scale, as a requirement names it ("Mathematics").

timing.description: When the course must be passed, for everyone; said after the text.

groups.description: Where one applicant group is told something else — SDU: from outside the EU/EEA, supplementary courses must be finished before 5 July.

text.description: Replaces the text for this group.

timing.description: Replaces the timing for this group.

multiple.description: Replaces the sentence about more than one course for this group.

afterResults.description: Replaces the count of courses allowed after the results for this group (SDU outside the EU/EEA: 0). Null: not recorded for this group.

quota2AfterResults.description: True only where a quotation says the institution's after-results route (conditional admission) applies to an applicant admitted in quota 2. Without it, a plan that needs a course after the results, for a student below the quota 1 floor, is "Needs review".

quota2Question.description: What a card asks where that is not recorded.

quota2AfterResults.description: True only where a quotation says the institution's after-results route (conditional admission) applies to an applicant admitted in quota 2. Without it, a plan that needs a course after the results, for a student below the quota 1 floor, is "Needs review".

quota2Question.description: What a card asks where that is not recorded.

afterResultsIfAccepted.description: Where `afterResults` is null (not recorded), the count that would apply if the unrecorded permission were given. A plan that fits only on it is "Needs review", never "possible".

unknownAfterResults.description: What a card says where the count is not recorded — "Whether this programme accepts summer supplementation is not recorded here — ask the institution".

afterResults.description: How many supplementary courses may be finished after the IB results arrive and still count for this intake (AU: 2; CBS: 0). Only where a quotation supports the number; without one the Recognition Scheme's applies. A plan with more courses than this is "Does not currently meet" for this intake.

multiple.description: What the institution says about taking more than one supplementary course (AU: at most two after 5 July). Without it the Recognition Scheme's national sentence applies.
